2. Push outward with your legs to engage the abductors while lowering your body into a squat position.
3. Return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and chest up during the squat motion.
2. Perform the movement in a controlled manner for better muscle activation.
Barbell Single Leg Hip Thrust
This is a unilateral exercise that emphasizes glute strength and balance while using a barbell for resistance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the ground with your upper back resting against a bench and a barbell placed across your hips.
2. Extend one leg straight out while keeping the other foot flat on the ground.
3. Push through your grounded heel to lift your hips upward, forming a straight line from shoulders to knees.
4. Lower your hips back down and repeat before switching legs.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep the movement controlled to prevent injury and maximize glute activation.
2. Use a barbell pad to make the exercise more comfortable on your hips.
Pelvic Tilt
The Pelvic Tilt is a bodyweight exercise that strengthens the lower back and engages the core and pelvic muscles.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
2. Engage your core and tilt your pelvis upward by flattening your lower back against the floor.
3. Hold the position briefly and then return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid arching your back during the movement.
2. Breathe deeply and maintain control throughout the exercise.
Glute Bridge One Leg on Bench
This variation of the glute bridge increases the challenge by isolating one leg at a time.
To perform the exercise:
1. Place one foot on a bench with the other leg extended straight out.
2. Push through your grounded foot to lift your hips upward, forming a straight line from shoulders to the elevated knee.
3. Lower your hips back down and repeat before switching legs.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to stabilize your body.
2. Avoid letting your hips sag or twist during the movement.
Unilateral Bridge
The Unilateral Bridge is a bodyweight exercise that targets the glutes and hamstrings while improving balance and stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with one knee bent and the other leg extended straight out.
2. Push through your grounded heel to lift your hips upward until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knee.
3. Lower your hips back down and repeat before switching legs.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain a slow and controlled motion for better muscle activation.
2. Keep your core tight to prevent any excessive movement or strain.
Side Bridge Hip Abduction
This exercise combines a side plank with hip abduction to target the obliques, glutes, and outer thighs.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a side plank position with your body in a straight line, supported by your forearm and the side of your foot.
2. Lift your top leg upward while keeping it straight.
3. Lower your leg back down without touching the ground and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to maintain a stable plank position.
2. Avoid letting your hips sag during the movement.
Straight Leg Kickback
This exercise targets the glutes and hamstrings by extending the leg backward in a controlled manner.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
2. Extend one leg straight back while keeping it in line with your body.
3. Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower the leg back down without touching the floor.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core tight to prevent arching your back.
2. Perform the movement slowly for better muscle activation.
Decline Bench Dumbbell Lunge
This exercise enhances lower-body strength and balance while incorporating the decline bench for added difficulty.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand in front of a decline bench, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Step backward with one foot onto the bench and lower your body into a lunge position.
3. Push through your front foot to return to the starting position and repeat on the other leg.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain an upright posture throughout the movement.
2. Keep your knees aligned with your toes to avoid strain.
Banded Standing Glute Kickback
This exercise uses a resistance band to target the glutes and hamstrings through a controlled kickback motion.
To perform the exercise:
1. Place a resistance band around your ankles and stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Shift your weight onto one leg and kick the other leg straight back while keeping it straight.
3. Return to the starting position and repeat before switching legs.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core tight to maintain balance.
2. Perform the movement slowly to ensure proper resistance and activation.
Banded Seated Hip Abduction
This exercise strengthens the glutes and outer thighs using a resistance band while seated.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on a bench or sturdy surface with a resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees.
2. Open your legs outward against the resistance of the band.
3. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and chest up during the exercise.
2. Use a band with appropriate resistance for your fitness level.
Banded Single Leg Glute Bridge
This exercise targets the glutes and hamstrings, with added resistance from a band for increased activation.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with a resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees.
2. Bend one knee and keep the other leg extended straight out.
3. Push through your heel to lift your hips while keeping the extended leg aligned with your torso.
4. Lower your hips back down and repeat before switching legs.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to avoid arching your back.
2. Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement for maximum effectiveness.
Banded Glute Bridge
This exercise enhances glute activation by adding resistance to the traditional glute bridge.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with a resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees.
2. Bend your knees and keep your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
3. Push through your heels to lift your hips while pressing your knees outward against the band.
4. Lower your hips back down and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid overextending your back at the top of the movement.
2. Focus on squeezing your glutes throughout the exercise.
Lateral Leg Swings
This dynamic stretching exercise helps improve hip mobility and warm up the glutes and hip flexors.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright with one hand on a sturdy object for support.
2. Swing one leg across your body, then out to the side in a controlled motion.
3. Repeat for the desired number of swings, then switch legs.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your movements controlled to avoid overextending.
2. Maintain an upright posture throughout the exercise.
Banded Walk
This exercise strengthens the glutes and outer thighs while improving lower-body stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Place a resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees.
2. Lower into a partial squat position and step sideways, keeping tension on the band.
3. Take a series of steps in one direction, then reverse.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and chest up throughout the movement.
2. Avoid letting your knees cave inward while stepping.
Band Side Lying Clam
This exercise targets the gluteus medius and outer thighs, using a resistance band for added intensity.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your side with a resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees.
2. Bend your knees to 90 degrees and stack your hips and feet.
3. Lift your top knee upward while keeping your feet together.
4. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat before switching sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to prevent rolling backward.
2. Perform the movement slowly to maximize resistance and activation.
Resistance Band Lateral Walk
This exercise strengthens the glutes, outer thighs, and hip stabilizers using a resistance band.
To perform the exercise:
1. Place a resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees.
2. Lower into a slight squat position with feet shoulder-width apart.
3. Step sideways with one foot, then follow with the other foot, keeping tension on the band.
4. Continue for the desired number of steps, then switch directions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your knees slightly bent and your chest upright.
2. Avoid letting your knees collapse inward while stepping.
Banded Glute Kickbacks
This exercise isolates the glutes and hamstrings, using a resistance band for added challenge.
To perform the exercise:
1. Place a resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees.
2. Get into a tabletop position with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
3. Extend one leg straight back, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
4. Return to the starting position and repeat before switching legs.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and avoid arching during the movement.
2. Focus on engaging your glutes rather than your lower back.
Banded Donkey Kicks
This exercise targets the glutes and hamstrings with added resistance from a band.
To perform the exercise:
1. Place a resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees.
2. Start in a tabletop position with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
3. Lift one knee and kick your foot upward, extending your leg straight behind you.
4. Lower your knee back down without touching the ground and repeat before switching legs.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid twisting your hips during the movement.
2. Squeeze your glutes at the top of each kick for maximum activation.
Banded Thigh Fly
This exercise strengthens the inner and outer thighs, glutes, and hips.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with a resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees.
2. Bend your knees, keeping your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
3. Open your knees outward against the resistance of the band.
4. Slowly bring your knees back together and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Engage your core to maintain stability during the movement.
2. Perform the movement slowly to maximize resistance.
Band Side Lying Leg Lift
This exercise targets the gluteus medius and improves hip stability with added resistance from a band.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your side with a resistance band around your ankles.
2. Keep your bottom leg bent for support and your top leg straight.
3. Lift your top leg upward against the resistance of the band.
4. Lower your leg back down in a controlled motion and repeat before switching sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid rolling your hips backward during the movement.
2. Perform the exercise slowly to maintain tension on the band.
Banded Fire Hydrant
This exercise activates the glutes, hip abductors, and stabilizers using a resistance band.
To perform the exercise:
1. Place a resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees.
2. Start in a tabletop position with your hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
3. Lift one knee out to the side while keeping it bent, resisting the tension of the band.
4. Lower the knee back down and repeat before switching sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back flat and core engaged throughout the movement.
2. Avoid rotating your hips during the lift.
Kneeling Jump Squat
This plyometric exercise builds explosive power in the lower body and glutes.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a kneeling position with your knees hip-width apart and feet flat on the floor.
2. Swing your arms forward and push through your hips to jump into a squat position.
3. Land softly with your knees slightly bent and return to the kneeling position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Engage your core to maintain stability during the jump.
2. Land softly to reduce impact on your joints.
Banded Kettlebell Goblet Squat
This exercise targets the glutes, quads, and hamstrings with added resistance from a band.
To perform the exercise:
1. Place a resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees, and hold a kettlebell at chest height.
2. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly turned out.
3. Lower into a squat, pushing your knees outward against the band.
4. Push through your heels to return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and chest up throughout the movement.
2. Avoid letting your knees collapse inward.
Kettlebell Front Squat
This exercise strengthens the glutes, quads, and core while improving squat mechanics.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a kettlebell in the rack position at shoulder height with one or both hands.
2. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly turned out.
3. Lower into a squat, keeping your chest upright and back straight.
4. Push through your heels to return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your elbows pointed forward to maintain proper kettlebell positioning.
2. Focus on engaging your core throughout the movement.
Single Knee To Chest
This stretch improves flexibility in the lower back, glutes, and hamstrings.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your legs extended and arms at your sides.
2. Bend one knee and pull it toward your chest, holding it with both hands.
3. Hold the stretch for the desired duration, then switch to the other leg.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your other leg straight and relaxed on the ground.
2. Avoid lifting your head or shoulders off the floor.
Pistol Squat to Box
This exercise improves single-leg strength, balance, and control while reducing the depth to accommodate different skill levels.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand in front of a box or bench with one leg extended forward.
2. Lower your body into a squat on the supporting leg until your glutes lightly touch the box.
3. Push through your heel to return to the starting position and repeat before switching legs.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your chest up and core engaged for stability.
2. Use a box height that allows for proper form without overstraining.
Frog Pump
This glute isolation exercise targets the gluteus maximus and medius with minimal strain on the lower back.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and the soles of your feet pressed together.
2. Push through your heels to lift your hips off the ground, squeezing your glutes at the top.
3. Lower your hips back down and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid overextending your lower back during the lift.
2. Focus on squeezing your glutes throughout the movement.
Landmine Deadlift
This variation of the deadlift uses a landmine attachment to target the posterior chain while reducing stress on the lower back.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand over the barbell with the landmine attachment, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Grip the end of the barbell with both hands and hinge at your hips to lower into a deadlift position.
3. Push through your heels to stand up, extending your hips fully at the top.
4. Lower the barbell back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the movement.
2. Avoid using your arms to lift the weight; focus on your glutes and hamstrings.
Band Seated Hip External Rotation
This exercise strengthens the hip rotators and improves stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on a bench or chair with a resistance band looped around your thighs, just above your knees.
2. Open your knees outward against the resistance of the band, keeping your feet flat on the floor.
3. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain a straight back and upright posture while seated.
2. Control the movement to avoid relying on momentum.
Band Seated Hip Internal Rotation
This exercise targets the hip internal rotators and enhances mobility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on a bench or chair with a resistance band looped around your thighs, just above your knees.
2. Rotate your knees inward against the resistance of the band, keeping your feet flat on the floor.
3. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Sit upright with your back straight to engage the correct muscles.
2. Move slowly and deliberately to maximize muscle activation.
Landmine Squat
This compound exercise targets the quads, glutes, and core while allowing for an upright torso position.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the end of the barbell with both hands close to your chest.
2. Lower your body into a squat by bending your knees and hips while keeping the barbell in front of you.
3. Push through your heels to return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your chest lifted and core engaged throughout the movement.
2. Ensure your knees track over your toes during the squat.
Rack Pull
The Rack Pull is a partial deadlift that focuses on the upper posterior chain, particularly the traps, lats, and spinal erectors.
To perform the exercise:
1. Set the barbell on a rack or blocks at knee height or slightly below.
2. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and grip the barbell just outside your legs.
3. Lift the barbell by extending your hips and knees until standing upright.
4. Lower the barbell back to the rack and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and shoulders retracted throughout the lift.
2. Avoid using excessive weight to maintain proper form.
Standing Knee Hugs
This dynamic stretch improves hip flexibility and balance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
2. Lift one knee toward your chest and hold it with both hands for a brief moment.
3. Release the leg and return to the starting position before switching sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain an upright posture and avoid leaning forward.
2. Perform the movement slowly to enhance balance and control.
Fire Hydrant
This bodyweight exercise targets the glutes and hip abductors, improving hip mobility and strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
2. Lift one leg out to the side, keeping your knee bent at 90 degrees.
3. Lower your leg back to the starting position and repeat before switching sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back flat and core engaged to avoid arching.
2. Focus on controlled movements rather than speed.
Snap Jumps
This plyometric exercise builds core strength and cardiovascular endurance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a high plank position with your hands under your shoulders.
2. Jump your feet forward toward your hands while keeping your core engaged.
3. Quickly jump your feet back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain a straight line from your head to your heels during the plank.
2. Land softly to reduce the impact on your joints.
Piriformis Stretch
The Piriformis Stretch targets the deep hip rotator muscle that can contribute to sciatic nerve irritation when tight.
This stretch helps relieve tension in the glutes and improves hip mobility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the floor with both legs extended
2. Cross one leg over the other, placing foot flat on floor
3. Gently pull knee toward opposite shoulder
4. Hold for 20-30 seconds then switch sides
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep back straight and avoid rounding spine
2. Adjust pull intensity based on comfort level
3. Breathe deeply to enhance muscle relaxation
4. Perform after workouts or during dedicated stretching sessions
Half Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
This stretch targets the hip flexors which often become tight from prolonged sitting.
It helps improve hip extension range of motion and posture.
To perform the exercise:
1. Kneel on one knee with other foot forward (90° angles)
2. Tuck pelvis slightly and lean forward
3. Squeeze glute of kneeling leg to enhance stretch
4. Hold for 20-30 seconds then switch sides
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep torso upright - avoid excessive forward lean
2. Place padding under knee if needed
3. Progress by reaching same-side arm overhead
4. Stretch both sides equally
Barbell Glute Bridge
This loaded hip extension exercise specifically targets the glute muscles.
It builds strength in the posterior chain while minimizing spinal loading.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on ground with shoulders against bench, barbell over hips
2. Drive through heels to lift hips until body forms straight line
3. Squeeze glutes at top position
4. Lower with control and repeat
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use pad or towel for barbell comfort
2. Maintain chin tucked to avoid neck strain
3. Focus on glute contraction rather than weight lifted
4. Progress from bodyweight to weighted variations
Cable Hip Extension
This isolation exercise targets the glutes with constant tension from cable resistance.
It helps develop mind-muscle connection with the glute muscles.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach ankle cuff to low cable pulley
2. Face machine and extend working leg backward
3. Squeeze glute at full extension
4. Return with control and repeat
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep torso stable - avoid excessive leaning
2. Use light weight to focus on proper form
3. Perform movement slowly with control
4. Alternate with other glute activation exercises
Cable Hip Abduction
This exercise isolates the gluteus medius to improve hip stability and strength.
It helps prevent knee valgus and supports proper lower body mechanics.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach ankle cuff to low cable pulley
2. Stand sideways to machine and move working leg outward
3. Keep toes pointing forward throughout
4. Return with control and repeat
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain upright posture - avoid leaning
2. Focus on moving from the hip, not the foot
3. Use light to moderate weight
4. Perform both concentric and eccentric phases slowly
Donkey Kicks
This bodyweight exercise targets the glutes, improving strength and stability in the hips.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
2. Lift one leg, keeping the knee bent at 90 degrees, until your thigh is parallel to the floor.
3. Lower your leg back to the starting position and repeat before switching sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core tight to avoid arching your lower back.
2. Perform the movement slowly for better glute activation.
High Knee Run
This cardio exercise engages the core, glutes, and legs while improving cardiovascular endurance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart.
2. Quickly alternate lifting your knees to waist level while pumping your arms.
3. Maintain a brisk pace for the desired duration.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Stay on the balls of your feet for quicker movement.
2. Keep your back straight and engage your core throughout the exercise.
Inner Thigh Side Stretch
This static stretch targets the inner thighs, improving flexibility and reducing tightness.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with your legs wide apart and toes pointing forward.
2. Shift your weight to one side, bending the knee while keeping the other leg straight.
3. Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and chest up during the stretch.
2. Avoid pushing too far if you feel discomfort in the inner thighs.
Plank Leg Lift
This isometric exercise strengthens the core, glutes, and lower back.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a forearm plank position, keeping your body in a straight line.
2. Lift one leg slightly off the ground, keeping it straight and engaged.
3. Lower the leg back down and repeat with the other leg.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid letting your hips sag or rise too high.
2. Keep your core tight to maintain stability throughout the movement.
Skater
This dynamic exercise improves agility, balance, and lateral strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a slight squat position with your feet hip-width apart.
2. Jump laterally to one side, landing on one foot while keeping the other leg off the ground.
3. Push off the landing foot and jump to the opposite side, repeating the movement.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Land softly to reduce impact on your joints.
2. Maintain control and balance during each jump.
Butterfly Stretch
This static stretch targets the inner thighs, groin, and lower back, improving flexibility and relaxation.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the floor with your legs bent and the soles of your feet pressed together.
2. Hold your feet with your hands and gently press your knees toward the floor.
3. Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds while breathing deeply.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid bouncing your knees to prevent strain.
2. Keep your back straight and focus on opening your hips.
Glute Bridge
This exercise targets the glutes, hamstrings, and core, improving hip mobility and strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground, hip-width apart.
2. Push through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
3. Lower your hips back to the ground and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to avoid overextending your back.
2. Squeeze your glutes at the top for maximum activation.
Arm Leg Raises
This exercise improves core stability, coordination, and balance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
2. Extend one arm forward and the opposite leg backward until both are in line with your body.
3. Lower them back to the starting position and repeat on the opposite side.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core tight to avoid sagging or arching your back.
2. Move slowly to maintain control and balance.
Dumbbell Forward Leaning Lunge
This variation of the lunge emphasizes the glutes and hamstrings while also working the quads.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand and step forward into a lunge position.
2. Lean slightly forward at the hips while keeping your back straight.
3. Push back to the starting position and repeat on the other leg.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your front knee aligned with your toes to avoid strain.
2. Engage your glutes during the forward lean for better activation.
Dumbbell Reverse Lunge
This lunge variation works the glutes, hamstrings, and quads while improving balance and coordination.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms at your sides.
2. Step backward with one leg and lower your body into a lunge position.
3. Push through the front foot to return to the starting position and repeat on the other leg.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your torso upright and your core engaged throughout the movement.
2. Ensure your front knee stays over your ankle, not beyond your toes.
Bodyweight Bulgarian Split Squat
This unilateral lower-body exercise targets the glutes, quads, and hamstrings while improving balance and stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand a few feet in front of a bench or elevated surface and place one foot behind you on the bench.
2. Lower your body into a lunge position, keeping your front knee aligned over your toes.
3. Push through your front heel to return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your torso upright throughout the movement.
2. Avoid letting your front knee cave inward; keep it in line with your foot.
Dumbbell Sumo Squat
This squat variation targets the inner thighs, glutes, and quads while engaging the core.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a dumbbell with both hands at arm’s length in front of you.
2. Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and your toes pointed slightly outward.
3. Lower your body into a squat, keeping your chest lifted and back straight.
4. Push through your heels to return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your weight evenly distributed through your feet.
2. Avoid rounding your back during the squat.
Hip Adduction Machine
This machine exercise isolates the inner thigh muscles, particularly the adductors.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the hip adduction machine and adjust the pads to your starting position.
2. Squeeze your legs together to move the pads inward.
3. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using momentum; move with control.
2. Maintain an upright posture with your core engaged.

Hip Abduction Machine
This exercise focuses on the gluteus medius and minimus, strengthening the outer hips and improving stability.

1. Control the movement to prevent swinging.
2. Avoid leaning forward or backward; keep your torso steady.
Zercher Deadlift
This unconventional deadlift variation emphasizes the quads, glutes, and upper back while improving core strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Position a barbell in the crook of your elbows and stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hinge at your hips and bend your knees to lower into a squat, keeping your back straight.
3. Push through your heels to stand up, keeping the barbell close to your body.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core braced to support the weight.
2. Avoid rounding your back during the movement.
Dumbbell Pull Through
This exercise targets the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back while engaging the core for stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a wide stance with a dumbbell placed on the ground between your legs.
2. Hinge at your hips and grab the dumbbell with both hands.
3. Swing the dumbbell back between your legs, keeping your chest lifted and back straight.
4. Thrust your hips forward to bring the dumbbell back to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid rounding your back; maintain a neutral spine.
2. Use your glutes and hamstrings to power the movement, not your arms.
Jefferson Squat
This squat variation targets the quads, glutes, and inner thighs while improving balance and core engagement.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand over a barbell with your feet shoulder-width apart, the barbell positioned between your legs.
2. Grasp the barbell with one hand in front of your body and the other hand behind, using an alternating grip.
3. Lower your body into a squat, keeping your chest up and knees tracking over your toes.
4. Push through your heels to return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep the barbell close to your body throughout the movement.
2. Maintain even weight distribution through your feet.
Glute Ham Raise
This bodyweight or machine-assisted exercise targets the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back.
To perform the exercise:
1. Secure your feet under a padded bar or similar support and position your thighs on the pad.
2. Start in a kneeling position with your torso upright.
3. Lower your torso forward by extending your knees while keeping your back straight.
4. Pull yourself back to the starting position using your hamstrings and glutes.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Move slowly and control the descent to avoid injury.
2. Avoid hyperextending your lower back at the top of the movement.
TRX Pistol Squat
This single-leg squat variation targets the glutes, quads, and hamstrings while improving balance and coordination.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold onto TRX handles and stand on one leg with the other leg extended in front of you.
2. Lower your body into a single-leg squat, keeping your extended leg off the ground.
3. Push through your heel to return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your chest lifted and back straight throughout the movement.
2. Use the TRX handles for balance, not to pull yourself up.
Sitting Wide Leg Adductor Stretch
This flexibility exercise targets the inner thighs, hamstrings, and lower back.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the floor with your legs extended wide apart.
2. Lean your torso forward while keeping your back straight, reaching toward the floor or your feet.
3. Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds and repeat as needed.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid rounding your back; keep it straight to deepen the stretch safely.
2. Breathe deeply to relax into the stretch and avoid bouncing.
Standing Wide Knees Adductor Stretch
This stretch targets the inner thighs and groin muscles, improving flexibility and mobility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
2. Bend one knee and shift your weight to that side while keeping the other leg straight.
3. Lean into the stretch, feeling a pull in the inner thigh of the straight leg.
4. Hold for 20-30 seconds, switch sides, and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and chest up throughout the stretch.
2. Avoid letting your bent knee extend past your toes.
Standing Wide Leg Adductor Stretch
This stretch focuses on the inner thighs and hamstrings, enhancing flexibility and balance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with your feet wide apart, toes pointing forward.
2. Hinge at your hips and reach toward the floor with both hands, keeping your back straight.
3. Feel the stretch in your inner thighs and hamstrings.
4. Hold for 20-30 seconds and return to standing.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid rounding your back; maintain a neutral spine.
2. Adjust the width of your stance for comfort and intensity.
Hip Circles
This dynamic warm-up exercise targets the hips, improving mobility and flexibility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hands on your hips.
2. Slowly rotate your hips in a circular motion, making large circles.
3. Complete 8-10 circles in one direction, then reverse the motion.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your upper body stable and focus on moving only your hips.
2. Perform the exercise slowly and smoothly for maximum benefit.
One Arm Kettlebell Swing
This exercise targets the glutes, hamstrings, and shoulders while improving grip strength and coordination.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and a kettlebell on the ground in front of you.
2. Hinge at your hips, grab the kettlebell with one hand, and swing it back between your legs.
3. Thrust your hips forward to swing the kettlebell up to shoulder height.
4. Control the descent and repeat for the desired number of reps before switching arms.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and avoid using your arm to lift the kettlebell; use your hips.
2. Maintain a firm grip on the kettlebell throughout the movement.
Resistance Band Overhead Squat
This exercise targets the glutes, quads, hamstrings, and shoulders while engaging the core for stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a resistance band overhead with both hands, arms extended.
2. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and toes pointing slightly outward.
3. Lower your body into a squat while keeping the band taut and your arms overhead.
4. Push through your heels to return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your chest lifted and avoid letting your knees cave inward.
2. Ensure the band remains taut and your arms stay fully extended throughout the movement.
Lever Standing Hip Extension
This machine-based exercise targets the glutes and hamstrings, focusing on hip extension strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Adjust the machine to fit your height and position yourself so the lever pad is against the back of your thigh, just above the knee.
2. Stand upright with your body facing forward, holding onto the machine handles for support.
3. Extend your leg backward, keeping your upper body stable and squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
4. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid arching your lower back during the movement; focus on glute activation.
2. Control the motion and avoid using momentum to lift the lever.
Wall Ball
A functional exercise combining a squat and an overhead throw, targeting the legs, core, shoulders, and arms.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand about two feet from a wall, holding a medicine ball at chest level.
2. Squat down, keeping your chest up and weight on your heels.
3. Explode upward from the squat, throwing the ball against the wall at a target height.
4. Catch the ball as it comes down and immediately move into the next squat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain a neutral spine and avoid leaning too far forward during the squat.
2. Use a controlled motion to catch the ball and transition smoothly.
Kicks Leg Bent
An exercise targeting the glutes and hamstrings, improving flexibility and strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart.
2. Bend one knee to a 90-degree angle, lifting your leg backward.
3. Extend your leg backward in a controlled motion, squeezing your glutes at the top.
4. Return to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid arching your back; focus on isolating the glutes.
2. Perform the motion slowly to maximize muscle engagement.
Kneeling Leg Out Adductor Stretch
A mobility exercise to stretch the inner thighs and improve hip flexibility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Kneel on the floor with one leg extended out to the side, keeping the foot flat.
2. Place your hands on the floor for support and gently rock your hips backward to deepen the stretch.
3. Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your extended leg straight and avoid rotating your hips.
2. Perform the stretch gently without bouncing to avoid strain.
Happy Baby Pose
A yoga pose that stretches the lower back, inner thighs, and hamstrings while promoting relaxation.
To perform the pose:
1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet lifted toward the ceiling.
2. Grab the outer edges of your feet with your hands, keeping your arms on the inside of your legs.
3. Gently pull your knees toward your armpits, keeping your tailbone on the floor.
4. Hold the pose for 20-30 seconds, breathing deeply.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Relax your shoulders and keep your head on the ground.
2. Avoid overpulling; focus on a comfortable stretch.
Kettlebell Figure 8
A dynamic exercise that improves grip strength, core stability, and overall coordination.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand.
2. Lower into a slight squat and pass the kettlebell between your legs, switching hands.
3. Guide the kettlebell around one leg and back through your legs, creating a figure-8 motion.
4. Repeat continuously for the desired number of repetitions, alternating hands.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and core engaged to avoid strain.
2. Use controlled movements to maintain stability.
Smith Machine Hip Thrust
A strength-building exercise that targets the glutes and hamstrings.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the floor with your upper back resting against a bench and a Smith machine bar positioned over your hips.
2. Roll the bar onto your hips, ensuring it’s padded for comfort.
3. Plant your feet flat on the ground, shoulder-width apart, and thrust your hips upward, squeezing your glutes at the top.
4. Lower your hips back down in a controlled motion and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid overextending your lower back at the top of the movement.
2. Keep your chin tucked and gaze forward to maintain alignment.
Resistance Band Hip Thrust
An effective exercise to activate the glutes and hamstrings using a resistance band.
To perform the exercise:
1. Place a resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees.
2. Sit on the floor with your upper back resting against a bench and feet flat on the ground.
3. Thrust your hips upward, pressing your knees outward against the band for added resistance.
4. Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower your hips back down and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged and avoid arching your back.
2. Ensure the resistance band provides adequate tension without slipping.
Resistance Band Hip Thrusts on Knees
A glute-focused variation performed on your knees with a resistance band.
To perform the exercise:
1. Kneel on the ground with a resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees.
2. Sit back onto your heels, then thrust your hips forward, pressing your knees outward against the band.
3. Squeeze your glutes at the top of the motion and return to the starting position.
4. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and avoid leaning too far forward.
2. Use a resistance band that provides enough tension for effective engagement.
Barbell Single Leg Deadlift
A unilateral strength exercise targeting the hamstrings, glutes, and core.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a barbell with both hands and stand on one leg, keeping the other slightly bent.
2. Hinge at the hips, lowering the barbell toward the floor while extending your free leg backward for balance.
3. Keep your back straight and core engaged as you lower the barbell.
4. Return to the starting position by pushing through your standing leg.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid rounding your back; focus on maintaining a neutral spine.
2. Perform the movement slowly to maintain balance and control.
Dumbbell Single Leg Deadlift
A unilateral exercise targeting hamstrings, glutes, and core, while improving balance and stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a dumbbell in one hand and stand on the opposite leg.
2. Hinge at the hips, lowering the dumbbell toward the ground while extending your free leg back.
3. Keep your back straight and core engaged as you lower.
4. Return to the starting position by pushing through the standing leg.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid rounding your back during the movement.
2. Move slowly to maintain balance and control.
Dumbbell Bench Squat
A lower-body exercise to strengthen glutes, quads, and hamstrings using added resistance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand and stand in front of a bench or box.
2. Lower your body into a squat, sitting lightly onto the bench while keeping your chest up.
3. Push through your heels to return to the starting position.
4. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using momentum to stand up; use controlled movements.
2. Keep your knees aligned with your toes during the squat.
Pendulum Squat
A machine-assisted squat variation focusing on the quads, glutes, and hamstrings.
To perform the exercise:
1. Position yourself in the pendulum squat machine with your back supported and shoulders under the pads.
2. Place your feet shoulder-width apart on the platform.
3. Lower your body into a squat by bending your knees and hips.
4. Push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid locking out your knees at the top of the movement.
2. Keep your back firmly against the support throughout the exercise.
Dumbbell Iron Cross
A shoulder and core exercise that improves strength and stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand and stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Raise your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the ground, forming a T-shape.
3. Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
4. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using momentum; keep the movement slow and controlled.
2. Engage your core to maintain proper posture.
Box Pistol Squat
A single-leg squat variation that builds strength, balance, and flexibility in the lower body.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand on one leg in front of a box or bench.
2. Lower your body into a squat, sitting lightly onto the box while keeping your free leg extended forward.
3. Push through your heel to stand back up to the starting position.
4. Repeat on the other leg.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use a box height that allows proper form without compromising balance.
2. Engage your core to stabilize your body throughout the movement.
Sitting Rotation Hip Stretch
A flexibility exercise targeting the hip rotators, improving mobility and reducing stiffness.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the ground with one leg bent in front of you and the other leg bent behind you.
2. Place your hands on the ground for support, keeping your torso upright.
3. Gently rotate your torso toward the front leg, feeling a stretch in your hips.
4. Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds and switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your movements slow and controlled to avoid overstretching.
2. Focus on maintaining good posture throughout the stretch.
Supported One Leg Standing Hip Flexor and Knee Extensor Stretch
An effective stretch targeting the hip flexors and quadriceps, enhancing flexibility and mobility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand near a wall or sturdy surface for support.
2. Bend one knee and bring your heel toward your glutes, holding your ankle with the same-side hand.
3. Keep your standing leg straight and your torso upright.
4. Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds and switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid arching your lower back; engage your core to maintain alignment.
2. Ensure you feel a gentle stretch without any discomfort.
Squat Mobility Complex
A dynamic exercise designed to enhance squat depth and overall lower-body mobility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Begin in a deep squat position with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
2. Place your elbows on the inside of your knees and gently push outward to open your hips.
3. Shift your weight side to side, forward, and backward to stretch the ankles and hips.
4. Hold the position for 20-30 seconds while maintaining a straight back.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid rounding your back; keep your chest up throughout the movement.
2. Move slowly and focus on areas that feel tight or restricted.
Side Lying Hip Adduction
An isolation exercise for the inner thighs, targeting the adductor muscles.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your side with your legs extended straight.
2. Cross your top leg over and place your foot flat on the ground in front of your bottom leg.
3. Lift your bottom leg upward, keeping it straight, then slowly lower it back down.
4. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions and switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using momentum; focus on controlled movements.
2. Keep your core engaged to stabilize your torso during the exercise.
Side Hip Abduction
A lateral movement exercise targeting the gluteus medius and hip abductors for improved hip stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your side with your legs stacked and extended straight.
2. Lift your top leg upward, keeping it straight and aligned with your body.
3. Slowly lower your leg back to the starting position.
4. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions and switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid rotating your hips; keep them stacked throughout the movement.
2. Perform the exercise with a controlled tempo for maximum engagement.
Side Lying Feet Raise
A strengthening exercise targeting the obliques and inner thighs, improving core stability and leg strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your side with your legs extended straight and stacked on top of each other.
2. Rest your head on your bottom arm and use your top arm for support by placing it in front of you.
3. Lift your top leg as high as possible while keeping it straight.
4. Slowly lower your leg back down to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your hips stacked to avoid rolling backward or forward.
2. Engage your core throughout the movement for stability.
Single Stiff Leg Deadlift With Resistance Band
An effective exercise for hamstrings, glutes, and balance using a resistance band for added intensity.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand on a resistance band with one foot and hold the ends with both hands.
2. Shift your weight onto the planted foot and hinge forward at the hips, extending the opposite leg backward.
3. Lower your torso until it is nearly parallel to the ground, keeping your back straight.
4. Return to the starting position by driving through your planted heel and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Focus on maintaining a neutral spine throughout the movement.
2. Keep a slight bend in your standing knee for stability.
Pull Through With Resistance Band
A glute and hamstring-focused exercise that enhances posterior chain strength using a resistance band.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach a resistance band to a low anchor point behind you.
2. Stand with your back to the anchor point and straddle the band, holding it with both hands between your legs.
3. Hinge at your hips, lowering your torso while maintaining a neutral spine.
4. Squeeze your glutes as you thrust your hips forward to return to standing.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid rounding your back during the hip hinge.
2. Control the movement to prevent snapping the band.
Swing | Gymstick
An effective full-body exercise targeting glutes, hamstrings, and shoulders while improving core stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold the Gymstick firmly with both hands, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hinge at the hips, lowering the Gymstick between your knees.
3. Thrust your hips forward to swing the Gymstick upward to shoulder height.
4. Allow the Gymstick to descend naturally, controlling the movement, and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Focus on using your hips for momentum, not your arms.
2. Maintain a neutral spine throughout the exercise.
Single Leg Reverse Hyperextension | Gymstick
A great exercise for isolating and strengthening the glutes and hamstrings, improving hip stability.
To perform the exercise:

Split Squat | Gymstick
A lower-body strengthening exercise that targets the quads, glutes, and hamstrings, performed with Gymstick resistance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Place one foot forward and the other foot back in a split stance, securing the Gymstick under your front foot and holding it across your shoulders.
2. Lower your body by bending both knees until your back knee is just above the ground.
3. Push through your front heel to return to the starting position and repeat before switching legs.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your chest lifted and core engaged for balance and stability.
2. Ensure your front knee stays aligned with your toes during the movement.
Squat | Gymstick
A foundational lower-body exercise targeting the glutes, quads, and hamstrings, enhanced with Gymstick resistance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, Gymstick secured under your feet and held across your shoulders.
2. Lower your body into a squat, keeping your chest lifted and back straight.
3. Push through your heels to return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your knees aligned with your toes to avoid strain.
2. Engage your core to maintain balance and stability.
Kneeling Single Leg Kick | Gymstick
An isolated glute and hamstring exercise performed in a kneeling position using the Gymstick.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach the Gymstick bands to your ankle and secure the Gymstick under your hands in a kneeling position.
2. Extend one leg back, keeping it straight and in line with your torso.
3. Return the leg to the starting position and repeat before switching sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to stabilize your torso.
2. Avoid arching your back during the movement.
Pin Squat
A strength-building squat variation that emphasizes control and power by pausing at the bottom of the movement.
To perform the exercise:
1. Set the barbell on safety pins at a height near the bottom of your squat range.
2. Stand under the barbell, positioning it across your upper back, and lift it off the pins.
3. Lower the barbell to touch the pins, pause briefly, and then drive upward to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your chest up and back straight throughout the movement.
2. Use the pause to eliminate momentum and build strength in the bottom position.
The Box Jump
A plyometric exercise for building explosive lower-body strength, targeting the glutes, quads, and calves.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand in front of a sturdy box or platform with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Lower into a partial squat and explode upward, swinging your arms for momentum.
3. Land softly on the box with knees slightly bent and step down carefully to repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Focus on landing softly to reduce impact on your joints.
2. Ensure the box is stable and at an appropriate height for your ability.
